note: Switch "convoys", Grain and the sea (off by default; island games only). Grain and silver cross the sea as convoys you can see on the map: bought grain, the fleet's winter grain and your allies' surplus sail to Syracuse; grain sails to your army on the coast; Carthage feeds its army and pays its mercenaries by sea. Each of your convoys is run by a contractor, the head of one of the rich houses, who may skim it. Storms take ships in winter, and an enemy fleet can catch a convoy with the same roll your fleet uses on Carthage's transports. The pattern is in the sources below (card docs/research/grain-and-sea.md); every rule and number here is invention.
landingNote: Ports in data/island.json, plus Gela and Acragas, which lie on the south coast: grain can be run onto their beaches. Leontini and the fortress at Aetna are inland, so an army there cannot be fed by sea.
